sp-spending-series.caption: State Pension spending, Great Britain and recipients overseas, 2022/23 to 2030/31
sp-spending-series.table_reference: Sheet: State Pension. Nominal terms block and real terms block, total rows; caseload block, total row.
sp-spending-series.qualifications: Northern Ireland is not included. 2022/23 to 2024/25 are outturn. Later years are forecasts made in spring 2026. Constant prices use the GDP deflator, not the Consumer Prices Index. Recipients are an average over the year.

sp-longrun.caption: Projected State Pension spending as a share of the economy
sp-longrun.table_reference: Table 3.1: Baseline primary spending scenario, row: State pension.
sp-longrun.qualifications: United Kingdom. A projection under stated assumptions, including that the triple lock continues. Not a forecast.

income-fifths.caption: Median weekly income after housing costs, by fifth of the pensioner income distribution
income-fifths.qualifications: United Kingdom. An average of the three years 2022/23 to 2024/25, in 2024/25 prices. Net of Income Tax and Council Tax. Fifths are formed separately for couples and for single pensioners. A pensioner unit is a single pensioner or a couple, so the couple figures are for two people.

observed-spending.caption: Average weekly spending of retired households, financial year ending 2025
observed-spending.table_reference: Table A23: High level expenditure by household composition.
observed-spending.qualifications: United Kingdom. Means across all households in each group. Housing leaves out mortgage interest and Council Tax, which are in 'Other expenditure items'. Health and education are not published for these groups, except that no household of two adults mainly dependent on state pensions reported any spending on education. So the categories do not add up to the totals. Two-adult households are not always couples.
columns: One person, mainly dependent on state pensions
Two adults, mainly dependent on state pensions

wealth-bands.caption: People aged 65 and over, by the total wealth of their household
wealth-bands.qualifications: Great Britain, April 2020 to March 2022. Accreditation of the survey is suspended. Wealth includes the home and private pensions. It does not include State Pension rights.
columns: Share of people aged 65 and over (per cent)
